perspective:
Vincent Chinana’s available information:

- He is a mechanic and longtime friend of Patrick Guzman, a construction worker. They met in their teenage years, share blue-collar work, and often collaborate.
- At the diner, Vincent asked Patrick whether he was really considering a new construction venture. Patrick said it seemed like a good opportunity to expand his business. Vincent said he had heard it was risky and asked if Patrick was sure. Patrick said he thought it was worth the risk but was still weighing options. Vincent expressed worry about financial security and suggested reconsidering or delaying until more information was gathered. Patrick thanked him and said he would think it over more.
- After a few days, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent said he felt Patrick was not telling him everything and that he felt betrayed as a friend. Patrick apologized, said it was complicated, said he had not wanted to worry Vincent with details, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- During their detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learned the investment troubles were serious. Patrick told him it had been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if things did not turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanked him and expressed gratitude.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent said the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick said it was starting to look up and that he was relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting him earlier and proposed a joint venture. Patrick agreed to work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick were optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent said their combined skills could make it successful. They began drafting a business plan, agreed to outline every step carefully, and agreed to cover all bases for success.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s unspoken thoughts, private reasoning, narrator-only labels, or any events/information not observed or told to him in these interactions.
